agenda_text:
AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
 verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
 glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
 using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
 archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 Library, Arts and Culture Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JANUARY 13, 2022 AT 9:00 AM

To help slow the transmission of COVID-19, and protect the health and safety of the community, City
Council, as well as Board & Commission meetings, will continue to be closed to the public for in-person
attendance.
The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social
distancing. Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and
AT&T U-verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed.

minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, January 20, 2022 at 2:00 p.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on January 20, 2022 at 2:00 p.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  •  The Agenda for the January 20, 2022 Regular Meeting was posted on January 13, 2022 on the
  Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  a. Minutes of the November 18, 2021 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission
  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Zadorian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Vice-Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

3.  INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal Arts and Culture
  Administrator.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones introduced Christina (Rhys) Chambers, Fellow from Coro Southern
  California, 2022 Fellows Program in Public Affairs; Ms. Chambers briefly explained her role in the
  Fellows Program in Public Affairs.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts
  & Culture locations.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker(s): None

5.  ACTION ITEMS
  a. Selection of a Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2022

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby appoints Commissioner Yank to serve a one-year
  term as Arts and Culture Commission Chairperson.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  1
 b. Selection of a Vice-Chairperson to serve a one-year term, beginning January 2022

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby appoints Commissioner Viar to serve a one-year
  term as Arts and Culture Commission Vice-Chairperson.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Zadorian, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

c. Storefront Art Program
  1. Motion approving the funding of a Storefront Art Program to produce temporary art exhibits in a
  retail storefront unit from January – December 2022 in an amount not to exceed $40,000 from the
  2021- 2022 Month Work Plan.

  •  Ms. Lopez provided a brief summary on the Storefront Art Program. The Commission asked
  questions and gave their feedback.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves funding of a Storefront Art Program to
  produce temporary art exhibits in retail storefront units from January – December 2022, in an
  amount not to exceed $40,000 from the 2021-2022 Work Plan, as more fully outlined in the January
  20, 2022 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Zadorian, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

d. Storefront Art Program – Temporary Program Consultant
  1. Motion approving the funding of a temporary program consultant from January – June 2022 to (1)
  work with City staff to develop the processes and procedures for a Storefront Art Program, and (2)
  liaise with artists to produce temporary art exhibits in a retail storefront unit, in an amount not to
  exceed $13,000 from the 2021- 2022 Month Work Plan.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Tufenkian

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves the funding of a temporary program
  consultant from January – June 2022 to (1) work with City staff to develop the processes and
  procedures for a pilot Storefront Art Program, and (2) liaise with artists to produce temporary art
  exhibits in a retail storefront unit, in an amount not to exceed $13,000.00 from the 2021- 2022
  Month Work Plan., as more fully outlined in the January 20, 2022 Report by the Library, Arts &
  Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Zadorian, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  2
   e. Claremont Graduate University – Work Study Program
  1. Motion approving the funding of a financial stipend for a Graduate student from the Claremont
  University - Work Study Program from January to December 2022 to assist with programmatic
  initiatives of the Arts and Culture Commission, in an amount not to exceed $7,000 from the 2021-
  2022 Month Work Plan.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves the funding of a financial stipend for a
  Graduate student from the Claremont University - Work Study Program from January to December
  2022 to assist with programmatic initiatives of the Arts and Culture Commission, in an amount not
  to exceed $7,000 from the 2021- 2022 Month Work Plan, as more fully outlined in the January 20,
  2022 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Zadorian, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  f.  Selection and Appointment of Commission Members to Artist Review and Selection Committees
  1. Motion appointing two Commission Members to serve a one-year term on the Artist Review and
  Selection Committee for the Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station & Storefront Art Program, Art
  Happens Anywhere, Brand Library Plaza Series & 222 East Concert Series, and Beyond the Box –
  Utility Box Mural Art Program.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Commissioner Tufenkian

  That regarding the Report to the Commission, dated January 20, 2022, about selecting and
  appointing Commission Members to the Artist Review and Selection Committees, the Commission
  hereby appoints two Commissioners to serve on the Artist Review and Selection Committee, for a
  one-year term, for each of the following Arts and Culture Commission programs and projects:

  1. Adams Square Mini Park Gas Station & Storefront Art Program
  Selected: Commissioners Zadorian and Tufenkian

  2. Beyond the Box - Utility Box Mural Art Program
  Selected: Commissioner Viar and Vidor

  3. 222 East Concert Series & Brand Library Plaza Series
  Selected: Chairperson Yank and Commissioner Zadorian
  Ayes:  Commissioners Vidor, Zadorian, Tufenkian, Vice Chair Viar, Chairperson Yank
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones provided updates on the AHA projects. The Commission asked
  questions and gave their feedback.

  3
   ii. LeBasse Projects – RFQ Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones provided an update on the RFQ applications. The Commission asked
  questions and gave their feedback.

  iii. Mural Ordinance - Community Input Meeting Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that the community meeting was held on November 17 via
  teleconference. She shared with the Commissioners community input and feedback.

  iv. The Aspire Group – Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones provided updates on the Aspire Group. The Commission asked
  questions and gave their feedback.
  v. Creative Crosswalks and Intersection Asphalt Murals- RFP
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones provided an update on the Creative Crosswalks and Intersection
  Asphalt Murals- RFP. The Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update
  3. PERFORMING ARTS – No Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update
  5. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS – Update
  • Staff will be drafting an RFP, in partnership with the Public Works department, to receive
  proposals from artists who have experience in asphalt art initiatives to design creative
  crosswalks located at specific intersections throughout the City. Staff will provide a draft RFP for
  review at the February 17, 2022 Regular Meeting. The Commission asked questions and gave
  their feedback.

7. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  • The Commission thanked ex Chairperson Tufenkian for her role as Chairperson for the Arts and
  Culture Commission and congratulated the new Chairperson Yank and new Vice Chair Viar.

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None

9. ADJOURNMENT – 3:16 p.m.

The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is February 17, 2022, at 2:00 p.m., via
teleconference.
